concerns.text: Centrality metrics are computed on a graph that includes all recorded channels (EEG Fpz‑Cz, Pz‑Oz, EOG, EMG). EOG and EMG are peripheral, non‑cortical signals; incorporating them into a functional‑connectivity network intended to reflect brain network topology conflates neural and non‑neural activity. This undermines the interpretability of degree, betweenness, and eigenvector centrality as *neural* predictors of sleep‑stage PLV and may introduce systematic bias. Consider restricting the network to EEG channels only, or at least reporting separate centrality analyses with and without peripheral channels.
